articleTitle: The choice of cable type for application at EHV system voltage
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The choice of underground cable type for EHV applications has increased as a range of new dielectrics has been developed. The authors consider the three types of single core cable now available for high power applications at system voltages of 220 kV and above: oil filled, paper insulated cable; oil filled, polypropylene/paper laminate insulated cable; and solid, polymeric insulated cable. Consideration is given to key aspects of EHV cable design and the choice of manufacturing plant required to achieve the necessary insulation quality. These aspects include features common to each type of cable, such as the need for large conductors, high insulation design stresses and metallic sheaths. A performance comparison is made between the three cable types based upon their current ratings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The useful life of plastic power cables with particular emphasis on the influence of humidity
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The cause of cases of damage resulting from the influence of humidity and electric fields in the polythene branched structures affected, the so-called water-trees, were studied. During this period (over ten years) several cable designs were developed with various protecting measures, as well as considerable efforts made towards improving the insulating materials and also to develop special materials less sensitive to water-trees. The published results of the investigations already indicate a considerable improvement of the materials and cable designs and in several fields there are also positive experiences in practical service. The resulting range of solutions and alternatives make the choice more difficult for the cable manufacturer, but particularly so for the user. The Datwyler company has performed long-term tests in order to select the most suitable material design for the insulation and to offer the highest possible operating reliability for the user. These tests have been largely completed and have produced results which can be clearly evaluated. The tests still in progress are only intended to provide better explanations of supplementary phenomena. The author summarises the most important findings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High temperature superconducting cable technology
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Having developed preliminary design concepts and investigated potential applications, EPRI is ready to launch a high temperature superconducting transmission cable R&D program which will lead to economically viable transmission cables of medium voltage for medium distances. The power capacity of the new cable designs is expected to range from 500 to 1000 MVA at 115 kV or 230 kV. Such designs enhance the prospects of matching, one-on-one, an underground transmission circuit to that of an overhead transmission line. This paper describes the design concepts in EPRI's program that would fulfill this objective and discusses potential applications for this new technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preliminary analysis of performance and cost of high temperature superconducting power transmission cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: After reviewing the technical performances and the initial economic assessment, based on a preliminary estimate of the expected cost of high temperature superconducting (HTSC) wires, the effect of the HTSC conductor cost on the economics of the power system is analysed, and associated breakeven values are evaluated for the current performance. These targets are taken as a reference for comparison with the state of the art of HTSC wires and for the evaluation of the specific progress required for developing economic applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cable rating methods applied to a real-time cable system monitor
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The authors outline how the National Grid Company (NGC) has a national scheme to provide cable system monitors (CSMs) installed in its area control centres. The CSMs provide online continuous and overload thermal ratings of cables based on system measurements and real-time thermal modelling, and enable the control engineers to assess the present security of the system and plan the operation of the system for the next day or possibly the following week. The CSM also holds archive data for retrieval and subsequent analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microphysical characterization of XLPE cable insulation after electrical aging
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Many different approaches to explaining the long-term degradation of polymeric insulating materials have been suggested, including chemical, electrical and mechanical processes. However, radial and angular variations observed in several physical properties of the polymeric insulation of cables often result from manufacturing processes, not from aging conditions. This paper reports many microphysical measurements on laboratory-aged and unaged cable samples: infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), density and dielectric relaxation spectroscopy. Variations in these characteristics have been recorded as a function of both radial and angular coordinates for XLPE power cable samples and, in most cases are found to be strongly correlated to optical birefringence measurements made on the same samples. However, in the case of dielectric relaxation measurements (time-domain-spectroscopy), the samples were not characterized by their birefringence values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reduction of AC-breakdown strength due to particle inclusions in XLPE cable insulation
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Addition of conducting iron and copper particles to XLPE power cable insulation reduced the short term AC breakdown strength from 107 kV/mm to 70 kV/mm and 35 kV/mm, for spherically and irregularly shaped particles respectively. In case of objects containing glass particles, the breakdown strength was reduced to 55 kV/mm, regardless of the shape of the particle. Addition of either 2,3 weight % acetophenone or cumylalcohol to objects containing 10 irregularly shaped iron particles increased the AC breakdown strength from 30% to about 80% of that of degassed reference objects without particles. Thus impregnation significantly reduces the detrimental effect of particles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An elastic joint for medium voltage power cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: In order to combine the main advantages of the pre-moulded slip-on joint and the heat shrinkable joint, a new joint, which is pre-fabricated and factory tested and that can be fitted at ambient temperature without tools over a large cable diameter range, has been developed. The new joint can also be used to connect paper insulated mass impregnated cables which are still extensively used in some countries (Italy, UK, Spain). As a consequence of the above designs a transition joint able to connect polymeric cables to paper insulated cables has been developed. The main features of this new generation of elastically recoverable joints for the voltage range from 12 kV up to 36 kV is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal performance modeling of power cable joints
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: A numerical model was applied to compare the thermal performance of two premolded power cable joint designs. High temperature gradient developed across the cable joint housing as a result of electrical connector degradation showed large differences between two designs; likewise, their temperature distribution at the outside of the housing also appeared very different. Consequently, this could cause inaccurate diagnoses if the surface temperature was used as the sole diagnostic parameter in the field monitoring with an infrared camera. From the results of the modeling calculations, a direct relation was established between the inside and outside temperatures of the housing for each design. This relation, together with the known conductor current intensity, could constitute a reliable diagnostic technique for power cable joints. Significance of the results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polymeric insulators for MV cable to overhead line connection
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: When underground cables are connected to overhead lines a number of basic functions must be fulfilled by the terminating device: electrical continuity from insulated cable conductors to (generally) uninsulated bare lines; sealing of the cable end against ingress of contaminants and environmental degradation; provision of insulating surfaces between live conductors and earthed parts of the cable or line support structures, that will remain stable throughout the life of the installation; and mechanical fixing of the component parts of the cable so as to provide support and prevent mechanical vibration from the line from passing into the cable. There is now a wide choice of terminating methods to accomplish these functions, but all are crucially dependant on effective outdoor insulation for a long and trouble free service life. The author examines some of the alternatives with particular reference to the use of polymers to supersede traditional outdoor insulation materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Long term testing of water tree retardant crosslinked polyethylene cable
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: There is a need for cables with water tree retardant (WTR) properties to increase confidence in long service life, particularly as cables can suffer mechanical damage during installation or service with treeing as a consequential result. Such a concern has been expressed by the Regional Electricity Companies (RECs) who are considering a change from paper to polymeric cables for medium voltage (MV) distribution. Long term testing is considered advisable to prove the permanence of the WTR and demonstrate the improved reliability needed to provide long service performance, particularly with regard to the growth of vented trees. The testing philosophy for such an assessment is being investigated by a number of workers worldwide and current European studies are leading towards test regimes with a 2 year duration. The authors describe the work carried out and give the results obtained in the extended test programme on the modified polymer option for WTR. Morphological aspects of water tree growth are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-frequency loss spectra and ageing in paper-insulated cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: This paper is concerned with a method for the assessment of degradation in underground paper-insulated power cables. One advantage of the proposed method is that less energy, and so lighter equipment, is needed to produce a transient than to sustain an alternating current in a long buried cable. Another is that the intrinsic loss at working voltage is derived independently of partial discharge activity (this is recorded and analysed more effectively by separate pulse counting methods). And finally, the measurement yields a spectrum of loss values over a broad frequency range, which affords more physical insight than a single-frequency measurement. The purpose of the present work is to develop the method for use with 11 kV and 33 kV cables, and to demonstrate the enhanced value of the low frequency spectrum in assessing ageing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a variable-frequency series resonant test set for after-laying tests on XLPE cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The first 132 kV XLPE cable in South Africa was installed in 1975/76 at Boksburg near Johannesburg. As a result of the experience gained in this plant, which was commissioned in 1979, it was decided at the planning stage of a second similar installation to purchase a fully type tested system of cable and accessories from one manufacturer and to carry out an AC after laying test. A transportable series resonant AC test set was purchased which operated at 50 Hz and was capable of testing up to 2 km of 132 kV cable at twice working voltage. Each 132 kV cable circuit on the second plant was tested at 140 kV, the highest voltage the manufacturer of the SF/sub 6/ switchgear would allow. Each circuit was tested for a period of 15 minutes. No failures occurred in test and there have been no failures of either cable or accessories since the plant was commissioned in 1981.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Endurance testing of XLPE cable insulation at extra high AC voltages
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) is used as insulation material in high voltage cables for voltages up to 275 kV. These cables are operating with an electrical field stress of approximately 10-12 kV/mm. To produce cables with an extruded insulation system for the 400-500 kV voltage range, an increase of the operating field stress to the range of 15-20 kV/mm is necessary. This is because of production line limitations, cable weight, dimension and cost. The main emphasis of this report is therefore on the capability of XLPE to operate satisfactorily for long time at extra high electric stresses. The authors focus on reduction of impulse breakdown strength, which is known to be an important measure of the lifetime reduction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new family of MV terminations
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: By using high dielectric constant and nonlinear resistivity stress relief systems, the stress at cable ends can be controlled without using the traditional stress cones. High dielectric constant and nonlinear stress relief systems use material characteristics and not shape, which results in a range of possible constructions that can be interesting when cables are terminated in applications with limited space or when cables vary in size. A big advantage of this technology is that it can be 'built-in' into materials like mastic, rubbers, etc. This means modern installation techniques like cold-shrink and slip-on become possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of medium voltage cable accessories for ease of installation
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The increasing use of polymeric cables together with a number of user trends has led to different criteria in the selection of accessories for medium voltage cables. In reviewing the above, it becomes clear that medium voltage cables accessories must be designed for simpler and more rapid installation requiring a low level of skill. After reviewing the various user preferences the choice of materials is discussed in detail, followed by a discussion of the development of two methods of terminating cables and a new joint design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of migration on the electrical properties of HV extruded cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Radial distribution of the electrical characteristics of HV XLPE insulated cables was investigated with respect to EEA or EBA oligomers migration into the insulation. During processing and aging, the migration of low molecular weight fractions of EEA or EBA copolymers used in semiconductive compounds gives rise to an increase of tan delta close to the semiconductive shields, and to a decrease of AC and DC breakdown strengths. However, this migration seems to increase the impulse breakdown strength, and to avoid bow-tie trees development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polypropylene paper laminate oil filled cable and accessories for EHV application
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Polypropylene paper laminate (PPL) insulation comprises an extruded sheet of polypropylene on either side of which are bonded two layers of thin paper. Although PPL has the external appearance of paper, its electrical and mechanical properties differ. It can be lapped onto a conductor and impregnated with dodecylbenzene (DDB) fluid using similar techniques to a paper cable. The authors initially summarise the advantages of PPL cable and the proving tests that have verified the performance of the cable and accessories. Accessory designs and the method of cable installation are described in detail. Finally the authors lists some current service applications of PPL cable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 245 kV XLPE cables as a mesh in a 220 kV overhead line transmission network
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The idea arose to feed the substations in the central parts of Stockholm with 245 kV XLPE cables and to equip the substations with 220/11 kV transformers of the same type i.e. two 11 kV windings and two 11 kV busbars. The author discusses the background to the project, project planning, load flow and short-circuit calculations, transient temperature calculation, cooling, induced voltages in communication cables, safety, and influence of arcs on cable faults.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of 500 kV low density polyethylene insulated cable
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Since 1969, the date of the first installation of 225 kV cables with low density polyethylene insulation (LDPE) SILEC have installed more than 1100 km of cable and about 4700 joints and terminations in 225 kV network in France as well as abroad. The in service results have allowed the development of LDPE insulated cables for the 400 kV and 500 kV networks. A feasibility study based on technical and economical considerations has led to the design of the 400 kV cable with a wall thickness insulation ranging from 27 to 30 mm, according to the conductor cross-section, and to the development of accessories, terminations and joints, made of high reliability prefabricated components. In the meantime, a 500 kV cable has been successfully tested in EDF laboratories and the first 500 kV LDPE link has been installed, energized and is now operating.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The HV transition joints
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: A transition joint between oil filled (OF) cables and synthetic cables with a similar design for voltages from 70 to 225 kV is presented in this paper. An original way of fitting both ends together has been developed consisting of: an epoxy resin insulator to separate both types of cables (classic); an OF fitting through the outer metallic housing; jointing by a plug-in connection system; and an outer metallic housing in 3 parts for an easy mounting. The paper describes the main characteristics of the HV transition joints range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of semiconductor impurity diffusion in XLPE cable insulation under electrical aging
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE)-insulated power cables exposed to a combination of high electric stress in the presence of water are susceptible to a form of degradation known as water treeing, which is largely responsible for the premature failures encountered in extruded HV cables. The present paper reports results obtained with both two-dimensional mu -PIXE (proton induced X-ray emission) scans and NAA (neutron activation analysis) measurements on a number of samples aged under different conditions. The impurity distribution in polyethylene insulation adjacent to the interface with the inner and the outer semiconductors was investigated. No convincing evidence was found of migration of impurities (atomic number>Na) from the semiconductor into the polyethylene insulation under electric aging conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Premoulded joints for voltages from 72 to 245 kV
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: This paper outlines a generation of prefabricated EPDM rubber slip-on joints. The fundamental advantages of this technique are complete production and testing in factory and quicker installation at site. The good experience in the MV joint, was the basis for transferring the existing know how to the high voltage range from 72 to 245 kV. In HV designs it is important to calculate the electrical and thermal constraints. The requirements on the materials are more important and also a clear insight in the molding process is necessary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of polyethylene based insulations for wet environments
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: There is much debate over methods used for testing medium voltage polymeric insulated cables for use without a moisture barrier. The proposals being considered by CENELEC for a European test involve ageing periods of long duration, up to two years. The cable is judged to pass if the breakdown strength is retained at a chosen level, or, if the test samples survive the ageing period. These tests will take more than two years to complete and report. Consequently there is a need for other assessments that could be used, possibly as sample tests, or even as pretest assessments. The author explores some of the factors that contribute to the test procedures and considers the prospects of quicker test methods. The author describes the role of temperature on the breakdown testing of tree retardant insulations; the influence of rapid temperature cycling on water tree growth; and the factors which influence vented treeing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Service experience with PE and XLPE insulated power cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: It is extremely hard to assess the working quality of cables with extruded insulation and to compare this with the traditional insulation of medium and high voltage cables. The reason is that the experiments concerning the PE and XLPE insulated cables began far later than the research related to paper insulated cables. However, from the perspective of 30 years experience with PE cables for 60 kV and 20 years with 225 kV cables, it is possible to speak well for their working parameters. Based on Swedish and Dutch research it is possible to state that the electric cables with crosslinked polyethylene insulation show high reliability. In Poland, PE insulated cables were produced for medium voltage in 1972, whereas medium and high voltage cables insulated with crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE), have been manufactured since 1988. The date presented concerns mainly PE insulated cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of moisture analysis for high and very high voltage XLPE and LDPE cables insulations
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: In France, high voltage cables with synthetic extruded insulation have been operated underground for about 30 years with a failure rate less than 0.2 defect/100 km/year. Thereby, diagnostic methods used after dielectric breakdowns showed that about 90% of the damages were caused by water penetration. Laboratory experiments showed that the presence of water trees was correlated with a large quantity of water in polyethylene insulation. That is why a development of moisture analysis of synthetic extruded insulations was made in laboratories in order to improve this method. The authors present the development of the experimental moisture measurement method applied to XLPE cable insulation of which water content was about 45-50 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 150 kV system for feeding Ischia Island
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Since 1951 until up to a few years ago, the growth of electrical demand on the Ischia Island (Italy) was met by means of MV submarine cable links. The present HV submarine cable connection represents an important improvement considering both total system reliability and power availability. This project was characterized by peculiar environmental conditions. On land, the discovery of Roman artefacts led the planers to look for a proper route and to adopt particular buildings for the plant concerned. In the sea, heavy traffic and fishing activities required protection of the cable at up to 100 m water depth, exceeding what is generally used. The authors describe how all the problems were solved thanks to a considerable coordination effort by all the project parties involved and to the proper solutions developed specifically for this project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of system and installation requirements on the introduction of 11 kV polymeric insulated cables in London
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: 11 kV polymeric insulated cables were first introduced onto the London distribution network in 1989, initially for specific projects but are now starting progressively to replace the use of the traditional paper insulated cable throughout the Company. London Electricity's existing 11 kV system imposes several restrictive operational and installation requirements which have significantly influenced the design of the polymeric insulated cable and jointing accessories. The authors describe the construction of a compact polymeric insulated cable system. In particular the cable includes solid aluminium conductors for compactness and galvanised steel wires to meet the earth fault requirements. These design features and the need for compact re-enterable joints have provided challenges regarding installation and materials compatibility which are addressed. The early operational experience with this type of cable and accessories is also briefly covered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of materials and design alternatives to service reliability of MV cables with XLPE insulation
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The authors describe the present state of experience with XLPE cables for medium-voltage in Germany. More than 20 years of operational experience with XLPE medium-voltage cables have proved the advantages during manufacture, laying, installation and operation. The well-known ageing processes could lead to an early failure of the dielectric system (insulation including semi-conductive layer) if neither design nor materials-related measures were taken. The operational experience in Germany and worldwide shows that other ageing processes which could influence the service life of XLPE cables are not likely to occur. Regarding the improved technology now available and quality awareness of manufacturers and users, that XLPE medium-voltage cables have the potential to reach the same service life as paper-insulated mass-impregnated cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and field experience with an HV-cable monitoring system
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The authors outline how, thanks to the development of a newly distributed temperature step-sensor, the thermal knowledge of HV cables may be improved, notably at the level of localized overloading in urban networks. The integration of such sensors in a cable monitoring system, including the measurement of various electrical parameters, allows the user to improve the availability of his power links and to reinforce the security as well as the flexibility of management actions, especially in the case of disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low smoke and fume cables with enhanced fire performance, resistance to moisture and mechanical properties
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: PVC (the traditional general purpose oversheathing material used in cables), when burnt emits large quantities of dense black smoke and hydrochloric acid gas arising from its decomposition mechanism in fire. Attempts to incorporate flame retardant fillers into PVC have been successful in limiting fire propagation but do little to minimise the problems of smoke and acid gas. As a result low smoke and fume (LSF) compounds were developed in the early 1970's. These compounds, however, have two major drawbacks: (1) poor mechanical strength; and (2) poor performance in water. In order to address these two limitations of LSF an intensive development programme was initiated, the results of which are discussed in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polymeric insulated high voltage cables and accessories in London's distribution system: a review of design, installation and performance
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Although, in relation to international usage, London's experience may be considered to be limited, variations in cable and accessories design philosophy have been produced by the UK manufacturers. The authors review the HV system design requirements for polymeric insulated cables and the economic factors influencing the type adopted, summaries the cable, joint and termination variations and the circuits installed to date in London. The performance of these circuits is briefly discussed and attempts are made to assess the likely future direction to be taken by London in respect of polymeric insulated HV cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short term and long term testing programme on 230 kV XLPE cable system
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The extruded cable system offers several advantages over fluid filled cable systems, arising mainly from the elimination of the insulating fluid and the associated disadvantages. There remain some concerns however regarding the long term service reliability as compared to that of the well proven and established technologies such as self contained low pressure fluid filled cables and high pressure pipe type cable systems. Short term and long term testing programmes go some way in increasing the performance confidence level for both supplier and user. The authors describe a series of short term and long term tests that have been carried out on a 230 kV XLPE insulated transmission cable system. The project brought together both European and North American philosophies in combination with experience and knowledge of a supplier and a user.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modern jointing system for medium voltage distribution cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The 11 kV distribution networks operated by UK Regional Electricity Companies (RECs) have for many years employed a bitumen-filled jointing system which has proved to be both reliable and cheap. The traditional jointing methods inherent in this system are, however, highly skilled, time-consuming and require the craftsmen to handle hot compound and molten plumbing and soldering metals. Alternative jointing systems have been available for more than fifteen years but RECs have been reluctant to change because the alternatives tended to be expensive and did not provide a full range of products. RECs were also conservative in their attitude towards change. Emphasis was placed on material cost savings rather than the effect any changes might have on the total installed cost. The authors discuss NORWEB's move away from traditional medium voltage jointing and the factors which were influential in the choice of a new system employing mechanical conductor connectors, heat-shrink insulation and resin encapsulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Environmental compatibility of supertension cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The need to minimise disturbance to the environment is an important consideration in the choice between overhead and underground transmission systems. The authors consider developments in the design of cable systems and their materials (paper, XLPE, polypropylene laminate). They demonstrate the choices available to the circuit designer and the improved environmental acceptability of underground transmission circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The anti-explosion HV and EHV terminations
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Generally, when there is an internal electric arc or a short-circuit in a porcelain termination filled by oil or SF/sub 6/ gas; the porcelain generally explodes and creates a significant amount of damage. The paper presents an anti-explosion porcelain termination design and the results of a short-circuit simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent technical trends of 500 kV XLPE cable
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The history, status and future development of 500 kV XLPE cables are described in terms of innovations in cable manufacturing technology. Consequent improvements in insulation design stress and cable life exponents, technical characteristics of 500 kV XLPE circuits in service and those now in the process of installation, and aspects of reduced insulation design are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prefabricated accessories for extruded polymeric cable at 66 kV to 150 kV
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Prefabricated accessories are becoming increasingly popular with users because it is perceived that the key jointing stage of applying the insulation has been simplified by using components that are moulded and routine tested under controlled factory conditions. This paper firstly considers the aspects of design and performance that influenced the choice of the composite type of prefabricated joint. Secondly it describes particular accessory designs together with manufacturing and assembly techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Drying of medium voltage cables-a chance to restore the electric strength?
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Many polymer insulated cables suffer from water trees when they are buried in the ground without a watertight shield. After some years in service the water trees may lead to a marked increase of the loss factor and to a decrease of the breakdown strength of the cables. To obtain informations on the drying and refilling phenomena the author took 10 m-pieces of field aged medium voltage cables (from three different manufacturers) containing water trees and examined the variation of the loss factors and the capacitances under various conditions over a period of more than one year. To simulate realistic conditions as close as possible, tap water was applied under the mantle of the cable but no water was injected into the conductor. This is a realistic simulation of a local damage of the jacket, whereby it is known that water flows very quickly along the cable. The applied voltage was 20 kV/sub RMS/, the frequency 50 Hz, and a conventional bridge was used for the measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fully water blocked 11 kV cable
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The ingress of moisture into 11 kV distribution cables, resulting from third party damage is a major practical concern to utilities. To address this problem a fully radially and longitudinally water blocked 3 core 11 kV cable with XLPE insulation and corrugated aluminium sheath has been developed. The design philosophy for the water blocked cable was to retain many of the features of an existing utility design whilst modifying the latter to offer both longitudinal and radial water blocking in all elements of the construction. The authors describe the development and testing of the new design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of Weibull statistical methods with other methods of data analysis (in power cable testing)
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The automatic use of Weibull statistics in testing power cables for electrical breakdown behaviour can lead to loss of information and unnecessary expense in experimental work. Here, the authors present a comparison of Weibull statistical methods with other methods of power cable testing data analysis, and show that by moving away from the Weibull assumption in such tests, the results can be more easily analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of the use of medium voltage polymeric cables for the distribution of AC power supplies to British Rail DC electrification substations
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: British Rail direct current electrification systems cover about 1800 route km of railway track in the south east of England and 170 route km in the area around Liverpool. The top contact third rail conductor system used is energised at a nominal voltage of up to 750 V DC supplied from trackside rectifier substations spaced at 4 to 7 km intervals. Generally, three phase 50 Hz power supplies are taken from the Regional Electricity Companies (RECs) at 33 kV or 11 kV and distributed via a trackside cable route to the substations so that, normally, each location is able to be supplied from at least two sources. Recent electrification schemes use subdistribution of 33 kV at a voltage of 11 or 22 kV. Typically, a REC will supply up to 6 substations, or 12 under abnormal conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of on-site partial discharge testing for transmission class cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Increasing installation of transmission facilities underground has led utilities to place greater emphasis on the qualification, acceptance and maintenance testing of high voltage cables. In particular, there is an urgent need for more searching probes of latent defects than are presently furnished by high voltage (AC or DC) withstand testing. As an alternative to this type of test, partial discharge (PD) testing can provide information on the existence of those latent defects known to cause premature in-service failure of high voltage cables. However, in order to realize the benefits of PD testing, the measurement system must be sufficiently sensitive, which implies for field testing, a high noise rejection capability. The present work addresses these key issues in designing a credible PD test for transmission class cables. The major noise sources are identified and methods to counter them are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning distribution systems considering thermal capacities of power cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Today, load forecasts urge the planner of electrical power supply networks to take extension measures according to common planning practice. To postpone or even avoid those decisions which are often based on too restrictive assumptions or too simple models is the main target of this study. This can lead to enormous savings in investment cost. Looking at the ageing process of energy cables in medium voltage (MV) networks possible transmission reserves are pointed out which are of main practical importance. The potential of these reserves can be quantified by using the authors' method to calculate the possible thermal cable capacity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Damage resistant armoured 3 core polymeric cables for medium and high voltage systems in the UK
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The authors address fault statistics at local and national level for cables between 11 kV and 132 kV. Areas of concern are highlighted in the apparent increased activity by utilities laying pipes, ducts and cables, giving rise to an increasing damage rate resulting in a need for a more resistant, robust cable better able to withstand the impact of tools. Various damage resistant cable types are discussed and the authors describe in detail the main design features, with reasons for selecting a 3-core armoured polymeric insulated configuration as the preferred choice. Experiences on new projects with medium and high voltage 3-core armoured designs are described. The authors conclude with valid reasons for selecting more robust cable types as the way forward to increase reliability of power supplies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 550 MW HVDC submarine cable link: Iceland-UK-continental Europe
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Iceland has an abundance of not yet utilised hydroelectric and geothermal power while there are potential markets in the UK and continental Europe for electric power. The authors present the results of investigations which show that power transmission by submarine cable to these markets is technically sound and that renewable power from Iceland can be transmitted and offered at prices which are firmly competitive even against gas generated power, the most economic low polluting source in the UK today. The resulting proposal for a 550 MW submarine cable link is also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cable System Monitor
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: The authors describe the Cable System Monitor (CSM) which has been designed to provide grid system managers with real-time computation of the load carrying capacity of selected cable circuits on the system. It was recognised that the increased thermal ratings that could be derived from the use of the CSM would defer capital expenditure, reduce generation restrictions or the need for running security plant and allow greater access to the system for construction and maintenance. Previous monitors provided a limited predictive capability. However, these simple representations needed to be developed into a more user friendly facility in terms of manipulating and shaping loading curves. The significant advantage with the new monitor is the ability to retrieve the archived loading history so that similar days can be compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design & installation of 22 kV power cable for London Underground Central Line refurbishment project
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: London Underground's Central Line refurbishment project encompasses the complete refurbishment of the line including the provision of new trains, signalling systems and power supply systems. The power supplies refurbishment concerns renewal of all life expired equipment and the enhancement of equipment to meet increased demands for traction loads to a peak service loading of 36 trains per hour and the upgrading of power feeds to maintenance depots. When finished the total project will have cost approximately Pounds 700 m of which approximately Pounds 50 m will have been spent on the power system refurbishment. The work has been conducted in three stages of which the last was the Eastern section from Bethnal Green substation to Epping substation which is the subject of this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MV cables with improved fire behaviour
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: An electrical cable with its linear characteristic and its function as a link has always been a transmission factor of fire from a point to another one, even if it is rarely at the fire origin. The cable makers' objective, as it has been for more than twenty years, is to reduce fire hazard due to cables. The authors describe the steps that have been accomplished today which include: reduction of fire propagation; reduction of rate and/or volume of smoke emission; reduction of halogenous materials, to minimize corrosion and toxic hazards; and use of halogen free materials. These improvements have been identified as a need by cable customers in different market sectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and use of a testing regime to predict life of premoulded rubber termination and connection products used on medium voltage power cables
publicationTitle: 1993 Third International Conference on Power Cables and Accessories 10kV - 500kV
abstract: Accelerated evaluations of current carrying systems are covered by thermal cycling tests of joints, splices and separable connectors as described in the applicable US and European standards. The applicable US standards are ANSI/IEEE Standard 404 and ANSI/IEEE Standard 386. A test regime, known as the 'multi-stress test' has provided the tool needed to evaluate designs of moulded rubber accessories. It provides an environment to better reflect actual use rather than simply using elevated voltage levels. The purposes of this test is to assess the dielectric integrity of the insulation system rather than the current carrying ability of the product. The primary goal of this paper is to fully discuss this test, its origins and future use. Short term production dielectric tests do not provide any significant insight into design life of a given product. The 'multi-stress test' provides a tool for qualifying new designs and processes for cable accessories in the same manner that cable manufacturers have adopted for cable in the US and Europe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
